Rationale for closing program: In 1993, the University of Rhode Island entered into a partnership with Rhode Island College to offer a Joint PhD program in Education.
Although the intention was for the universities to share the responsibility (budget, staffing, etc.), Rhode Island College has not, in recent years, been in a position to support half of the program responsibilities.
As such, the program has largely been supported by URI (teaching faculty, graduate assistants, travel funding, etc.).
Yet, most of the tuition revenue has flowed to Rhode Island College.
In the summer of 2022, the Deans of the URI Alan Shawn Feinstein College of Education and Professional Studies (Dennis) and RIC Feinstein College of Education and Human Development (Dingus-Eason) agreed to discontinue the current Joint Program.
Faculty and students have been notified of the decision to discontinue the joint program and a teach out plan has been developed.

Dean Dennis has also been working with URI OGC to ensure that the process aligns with the agreements between URI and RIC.
The agreement between URI and RIC states that “The continuation of this program depends on the continued agreement, support, and participation of both institutions.
Termination or withdrawal of support of the program at either institution will result in termination of the program” (p. 86).
As such, the faculty in the school of education have re-designed a stand-alone Ph.D. program in Education at the University of Rhode Island.
The program proposal for that “new” program is being submitted concurrently with this closure paperwork. (See Kuali) URI Faculty have used the “best of” current courses to design a scholarly doctoral program that is more research intensive than the current joint program–which was initially designed to prepare educational practitioners.
The proposed new URI program builds on current strengths (courses, faculty, ongoing research) to produce educational scholars who can solve the most intractable contemporary education problems.

The new program will allow students to develop focused expertise in an area of PreK-20 or adult education settings that aligns with current graduate program offerings and faculty expertise in the School of Education. 13.

FSEC charged CBUM with examining the policies relating to minor fields of study andUndergraduate Certificate Programs, as they are codified in the UM, and to bring forthrecommendations to the Faculty Senate.
